study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Lin et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2023
study_identification_part.si4_title: Understanding the heterogeneity of dynamic functional connectivity patterns in first-episode drug naïve depression using normative models

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Combine dynamic resting-state fMRI features with normative modeling to quantify and map individual-level heterogeneity in first-episode drug-naïve major depressive disorder (FEDN-MDD).
study_characteristics_part.sc2_study_design: Cross-sectional, multi-site observational study with normative modeling trained on healthy controls and applied to independent patients and controls from the same dataset.
study_characteristics_part.sc3_study_design_other: Healthy controls split into healthy-ICA (n=125) for network derivation, healthy-base (n=289) for normative training, and healthy-comparison (n=418) for application; patients FEDN-MDD (n=274).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Explored association between abnormal functional connectivity and symptom severity; no significant relationships detected.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Dynamic FC-based normative deviations distinguish distributions between FEDN-MDD and controls more than static FC; more patients show extreme supra-normal dynamic variability within networks; excluding top-5% outliers reduces case–control differences.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: - A greater proportion of FEDN-MDD show extreme dynamic variability across ≥100 connectivities (4.74%) than controls (3.35%).; - Network fluctuation deviations differ in DMN, left ECN, and limbic circuits, largely driven by male patients.; - Static FC group differences diminish after excluding top 5% "outliers" defined by number of deviations, suggesting case–control effects can be driven by a small subset.; - Distributions of supra- vs infra-normal deviations are comparable overall, with a shift toward supra-normal in controls for static FC; dynamic FC exhibits more patient skew.; - Sex-stratified analyses show differing deviation patterns across networks.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Limited symptom measures constrained detection of brain–symptom relationships; potential over-reliance on outlier-driven effects in case–control comparisons.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: we failed to detect the relationships between abnormal functional connectivity with the severity of depressive symptoms. We believed this was confined by the limited measurements of symptoms.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Defined "outliers" as top 5% by number of deviations and excluded them for secondary case–control analysis; normative modeling complements classical analyses by mapping individual deviations.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Multi-site rs-fMRI data with varied scanner parameters (see Table S1 in supplementary).
